title: Verbal-Promise Ledger for Mine Community Relations
one_liner: A voice-first, offline-capable phone tool that turns every promise a mine makes at community assemblies (Spanish, Quechua, Aymara) into a tracked commitment register the community can verify by WhatsApp.
customer: Heads of social performance and community relations at mid-tier copper and lithium operators and developers in Peru, Chile, Argentina and Bolivia. The second buyer is the E&S team at the lender or DFI (IFC, EXIM, DFC, export credit agencies). Budget is roughly $2-6k per month per project, charged to a risk or permitting line, not to IT.
problem: Insiders know that projects get blockaded over small, forgotten verbal promises, not over the headline issue. Examples are a promised well repair, a local-hire quota, or a dust-suppression schedule. The promise is made at a 2pm assembly and recorded on a paper acta, in a notebook, or in a WhatsApp voice note. Community-relations staff rotate every 12-24 months, contractors make their own promises, and nobody indexes the actas. Two years later the community says 'you promised' and shuts the road. The Las Bambas corridor closures, Jujuy lithium protests and Tia Maria all fit this pattern of trust debt. The mine cannot prove what it did or did not commit to, and neither can the community.
solution: Field officers record assemblies on a phone and snap a photo of the signed acta. Speech-to-text, tuned for Andean Spanish and human-checked for Quechua and Aymara, extracts discrete commitments: who promised what, to whom, and by when. Each one is assigned an internal owner and a due date. Community leaders get a receipt as a WhatsApp voice note or pictogram and can confirm, dispute, or mark it done. Ops managers and the CFO see 'commitment debt' aging, like a technical-debt dashboard. One-click exports meet IFC Performance Standard 1 and Equator Principles grievance and commitment register requirements. Community-side verification is the moat. It makes this a trust tool, not a surveillance tool.
why_now: Speech models are good enough for accented, code-switched Spanish, and usable for Quechua with a human in the loop. WhatsApp is universal in rural Andean communities. Lenders are demanding auditable social-license evidence for critical-mineral financings, including EU CRMA strategic projects and US DOE/DFC/EXIM deals. Argentina's RIGI regime is pulling lithium and copper projects into provinces with little consultation history. Peru and Chile have changed governments (2026), which reopens community negotiations. Staff turnover after the 2024-25 cost-cutting rounds has made institutional memory worse.
revenue_model: SaaS at $2-6k per month per project, plus a per-community onboarding fee ($1-3k). A one-off 'commitment debt audit' of historical actas is priced at $5-15k. Later, a lender-grade verified engagement score and a lender or insurer data licence.
non_obvious_insight: Conflict risk is mostly commitment debt, meaning unanswered small promises lost through staff rotation, not big ideological opposition. Buyers think they need sentiment analysis. What they need is a receipt system. Giving the community the receipt is what makes the mine's data credible to lenders and inspectors.
first_30_days: Through ex-colleagues, recruit two junior or mid-tier developers currently in a consultation round. Sell a $5-10k 'commitment debt audit': scan their last 12 months of actas and meeting minutes, and use an LLM plus a local linguist to extract every commitment and flag the overdue ones. This works with no integration, just PDFs and photos. The overdue list is usually shocking, and it converts to a SaaS pilot for the next assembly round. Use a WhatsApp Business API bot and an offline recorder app for v1. Do not build a custom platform yet.

title: PFAS-Cleared Succession for Plating Shops
angle: Pairing 2: Manufacturing reshoring/tariffs x Water infrastructure
one_liner: Fixed-price wastewater and PFAS readiness reports that let retiring plating and anodizing owners sell to buyers and lenders, feeding a buyer marketplace.
customer: Retiring owners of metal-finishing shops, industrial business brokers, SBA lenders and search-fund or roll-up buyers, at $9-18k per report plus a success fee.
problem: About 60% of manufacturing firms have owners aged 55+, and reshoring and defense customers cannot find finishing capacity (plating, anodizing, passivation). Wet-process shops carry discharge permits, sludge records and historic PFAS exposure that stall buyers' and lenders' diligence, so shops close instead of transferring.
solution: A standardized wet-shop report covering permit and sewer-use history, a PFAS use inventory and sampling, sludge manifests and quoted closed-loop upgrades. Add a clean-up and certification package, then match certified shops to buyers.
why_now: Reshoring is happening inside existing buildings. POTWs are hunting PFAS sources ahead of 2027 monitoring. Compass-type roll-ups are buying shops, and the MMS admits no dataset of owners near retirement exists.
revenue_model: Report fee, 1% success fee on transactions, and remediation referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: The real reshoring bottleneck is finishing, not machining. Finishing shops cannot change hands because water liabilities are unpriced, so whoever prices them owns the deal flow.
first_30_days: Call 10 industrial business brokers and the metal-finishing trade association. Do two discounted reports. Publish a one-page checklist to build a lead list of owners.

title: 48-Hour Patent Troll Response Desk for SMBs
one_liner: A flat-fee service that answers patent-troll demand letters within 48 hours with an AI-built claim chart, prior art, the assertion entity's litigation history and an attorney-signed response.
customer: Small e-commerce, restaurant-tech, app and SaaS companies (under about $20M revenue) receiving non-practicing-entity demand letters or complaints, plus IP insurers and trade associations that want a member benefit.
problem: Trolls price demands just below the cost of defense ($50k to $150k+), betting small targets will settle. Hourly-billing law firms can't respond cheaply, and the patent office's post-grant review path has gotten harder since 2025 with rising discretionary denials, though a March 2026 USPTO memo added small-business and domestic-manufacturing factors.
solution: 24-hour intake. LLM-assisted claim mapping of the patent to the target's product, a prior-art sweep, the patent's history (past invalidations, review petitions, family members, assignment chain), and the plaintiff's prior settlement pattern from court dockets. A partner patent attorney reviews and signs a response letter. Options: a shared 'campaign file' for other targets of the same troll, and an insured defense fund via membership.
why_now: Modern models can chart claims and search prior art in hours rather than billable weeks. Incumbent firms, paid by the hour, have little incentive to compress. The patent office's shifting policies make cheap district-court leverage more valuable.
revenue_model: Fixed $2.5k to $6k per response package, $99 to $299 monthly membership with pooled defense credits, and referral or insurance partnerships.
non_obvious_insight: The troll's model relies on low-cost, repeated assertion against many small targets, so it is undermined by a cheap, credible response and by a memory of it. Every response feeds a campaign file, and the second, third and hundredth target of the same entity get better and cheaper defense. That flips the network effect from the troll to the defenders, and word spreads fast that a target is not a soft settle.
first_30_days: Partner with one patent litigator on a flat-fee arrangement. Pull the top 20 active NPE campaigns from court dockets and pre-build claim-chart templates. Announce free 24-hour triage in small-business, Shopify and app-developer communities. Charge $3k for the first five full response packages.

title: Pay Home Inspectors to Find Lead Pipes
one_liner: A micro-bounty network that pays home inspectors, plumbers and water-heater installers to photograph where the service line enters the basement, with AI classification, so utilities can clear 'unknown material' lines for about $40 each instead of $500-3,000 each.
customer: Mid-size municipal and district water utilities (20k-300k connections) with a large 'unknown material' share in their published lead service line inventory. The buyer is the utility director or the lead program manager. A secondary payer is the home buyer, who pays about $29 for a 'Lead Line Certificate' add-on at inspection.
problem: Since the lead and copper inventory requirement, every system has had to classify each service line as lead, galvanized-requiring-replacement, non-lead or unknown. Unknowns are a legal and financial liability, and they are hard to shrink. The only sure verification is potholing or excavation, which costs hundreds to thousands of dollars per line. Customer self-ID by mailer gets a response rate of roughly 10-25%. Absentee landlords and LLCs almost never answer. Utility crews can't look inside private basements, so tens of thousands of unknowns sit in the spreadsheet for years.
solution: A mobile app with a fixed 3-photo protocol: the pipe where it enters the building, a scratch or magnet test close-up, and the meter serial number with the address. A vision model classifies the pipe as copper, galvanized, lead, PEX, PVC or HDPE, or flags it as unresolved. Humans QA the low-confidence cases. Each submission is geo-verified and tamper-evident, and exports in the format the state inventory portal expects. Inspectors and plumbers earn $15-25 per verified line, and the platform earns the spread. The utility gets a reconciled inventory feed and a dashboard showing unknowns falling by ZIP code. The consumer add-on (inspector-branded certificate, sold to the buyer) pays the inspector while giving the utility free data.
why_now: The first inventories were filed in late 2024, and public analyses showed millions of lines still classified 'unknown'. The Lead and Copper Rule Improvements set a 10-year replacement clock that starts around 2027, though federal details keep being revisited and litigated. Several states have their own replacement statutes that don't depend on the federal rule. The $15B in dedicated infrastructure-law lead line money is moving through state revolving funds under spend-down pressure. Vision models are only now accurate enough to classify pipe photos. (Regulatory details are from memory. Verify state acceptance rules before pitching.)
revenue_model: Utilities pay $30-60 per verified line, sold as a per-line contract that fits under small-purchase thresholds. A $10-25k pilot is typical, followed by annual contracts. The consumer-paid certificate ($29) is split with the inspector. Later products are inventory-reconciliation SaaS and an access-agreement workflow for replacement crews.
non_obvious_insight: Utilities think they have a data problem, but they have an eyeballs-in-basements problem. Every home sale (an inspector visits) and every water heater swap (a plumber stands three feet from the service entry) already puts a paid expert next to the exact pipe that matters. Nobody has paid them for a photo yet. Excavation is the wrong tool for a question that visual inspection answers for almost nothing.
first_30_days: Pick one state that accepts documented visual or contractor verification. Pick two utilities in it whose public inventories are more than 40% unknown. Recruit 30 inspectors through local InterNACHI and ASHI chapter meetups and Facebook groups, and pay a launch bonus per photo set. Run a 200-line pilot. Have the utility pothole 30 of those lines as ground truth, then publish the accuracy numbers. Close a $15-25k pilot purchase order with the first utility, using the small-purchase limit that many cities set at $25-50k so no council vote is needed.

title: Archival Footage Authenticity Clearance for Documentaries
one_liner: A per-film clearance service that proves each archival still and clip is real, so producers and E&O insurers can sign off.
customer: Independent documentary producers, YouTube documentary channels and news video teams, plus clearance consultants and E&O brokers that refer them.
problem: Clearance houses check rights, not reality. Stock libraries and search results now contain AI-made 'archival' images, and one fake in a true-crime doc becomes a public scandal, as with the AI images alleged in Netflix's What Jennifer Did (2024). E&O underwriters ask for clearance procedures. Visible AI watermarks are unreliable, since removers for Sora output appeared within a week of its launch.
solution: Fixed-price audit of a film's cut list. For each asset: trace it to the earliest source via reverse search and archive catalogs, run metadata and codec forensics, check C2PA and SynthID where available, run a detector ensemble, and produce a provenance chain. Deliver a per-asset source dossier and a producer's memo formatted for insurers and distributors. A portal re-checks only assets that change between cuts.
why_now: Sora's shutdown (app Apr 26, API Sep 24) removes one source, but open video models keep flooding stock sources. Streamers publish AI guidelines, and TikTok's C2PA membership in Jul 2026 normalizes provenance checks.
revenue_model: $1.5-10k per film, $500-3k/month for YouTube documentary or news teams, and referral fees from clearance consultants.
non_obvious_insight: Rights clearance is already a budgeted line item in every documentary. Authenticity clearance is a new column in an existing spreadsheet, so it does not need a new budget line.
first_30_days: Reach five documentary producers via the International Documentary Association and doc-maker Slack groups. Run a free audit on one recently published film's archival section, partner with two clearance consultants for referrals, and charge $2.5k for the next five.

title: Proof-of-Workout Fraud Shield for Fitness Incentives
one_liner: A verification API that scores whether a gym visit or workout really happened, priced per verified event.
customer: Administrators of pay-per-visit fitness benefits (regional Medicare Advantage plans, employer stipend platforms), movement-reward and fitness-betting apps.
problem: Chain: Medicare Advantage plans are trimming fitness benefits (93 percent offered one in 2026 versus 95 percent in 2025, more cuts expected) and payers and employers shift toward pay-per-verified-visit and reward models (one employer wellness network lists over 20,000 employer partners), so money follows check-ins and step counts. Fraud (shared QR codes, spoofed steps, ghost visits, inflated gym counts) becomes the margin killer and nobody sells fraud scoring built for fitness.
solution: An SDK and API combining phone attestation, gym BLE or Wi-Fi beacons, wearable heart-rate and motion consistency, GPS and barometer, and device-sharing graphs into an authenticity score with an audit trail, ring detection and a dispute workflow for gyms.
why_now: Benefit cuts push payers to pay-per-use, wearable aggregator APIs make cross-signal checks cheap, and mobile attestation is mature; HIPRA-style consent rules make audit trails a requirement.
revenue_model: $0.05-0.20 per verified event with a $2-5k monthly minimum, plus a gain share on recovered fraud.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is a labeled fraud dataset: once you process millions of visits you can sell audits to payers, and because you are neutral infrastructure you compete with no wearable or gym software vendor.
first_30_days: Find 2-3 reward or betting apps or one regional benefit administrator, run their last 90 days of check-ins through a prototype scorer, quantify suspected fraud, and charge $5-10k for the audit before integrating.

title: Surge Beds: Pre-Contracted Lodging for Catastrophe Responders
one_liner: Sell adjuster firms and storm contractors reserved-bed options on inland RV pads, seasonal parks and closed motels, contracted before landfall at prices that stay legal after an emergency declaration.
customer: Independent-adjuster firms' cat operations and logistics managers, restoration franchisees, roofing and mitigation contractors bringing out-of-state crews, and utility subcontractors. Reservation fees are paid pre-season, activation nights after the event.
problem: After landfall or a big wildfire, responder capacity is limited by beds, not people. Adjusters sleep in cars, 90 minutes away, or in RVs on borrowed lots, and deployed adjusters quit or rotate out. Anti-gouging laws (34 states, typically capping increases at about 10% for 30 days after a declaration) stop hotels from raising rates, so price cannot allocate scarce rooms; they simply sell out to whoever had a relationship or a corporate block.
solution: A lodging-capacity option network. Sign inland owners 60-150 miles from likely landfall zones (seasonal RV parks and park-model communities that sit empty in hurricane season, church halls and school gyms, closed-for-season motels, dorms, and short-term-rental owners willing to accept 30-day minimum stays) to pre-agreed rates that are lawful because they were set before the emergency. Buyers pay a per-bed or per-site reservation fee before the season, credited against activation nights. Add paid extras that responders actually need: Starlink, laundry, catering, portable showers, secure parking for trucks and trailers. Extend to wildfire base camps in CA, OR and CO.
why_now: Quick searches surfaced no dedicated adjuster-lodging option marketplace, only ad hoc use of RV parks after storms like Michael. Two years of quiet U.S. hurricane landfalls (none in 2025, and no hurricane at all in the 2026 Atlantic season through Sept 11) mean firms have not tested surge logistics and will be caught out by the next big one. Adjuster and contractor headcounts are being squeezed by automation and tight margins, so a predictable per-bed cost is more attractive than scrambling. Anti-gouging enforcement has grown more aggressive.
revenue_model: Reservation fees of roughly $400-$900 per bed per season, credited against activation nights. On activation, a 15-20% margin over the pre-agreed owner rate, plus ancillary services (connectivity, meals, laundry) at 30-40% margin. Later, annual enterprise contracts with IA firms for guaranteed headcount blocks.
non_obvious_insight: Because gouging laws freeze price after the declaration, the only legal way to buy certainty is to contract early, which turns lodging into an options market where the option seller (a snowbird RV park empty from June to October) has almost no other use for its inventory in exactly the months responders need it. Insiders know the constraint on a cat deployment is where 200 adjusters sleep, not how many exist.
first_30_days: Call 50 seasonal RV parks, campgrounds and small motel owners across the inland Gulf Coast, Carolinas and Texas and sign non-binding LOIs on rates and bed counts. Draft a one-page option contract reviewed by a hospitality lawyer for gouging-law compliance. Pitch logistics managers at 8 IA firms and restoration franchise groups on 2027 pre-season blocks, aiming for 2-3 signed reservation deposits of 20-50 beds each. Build a simple booking and check-in app with texted access codes and a map of inventory.

title: Toddler Talk: Voice-Based Developmental Screening
one_liner: A phone-recorded three-minute parent-child talk sample plus automated screening workflow that helps pediatric practices catch speech and developmental delays earlier and capture reimbursement.
customer: Pediatric practices and health systems (developmental screening is billable under CPT 96110), Early Intervention programs and Medicaid managed care plans.
problem: Speech-language delay is a very common developmental issue, but screening relies on parent questionnaires with modest sensitivity, practices under-screen and Early Intervention waitlists are long. Kids are referred late.
solution: Phase 1 (no diagnostic claims) is a text-based well-visit screening workflow that increases completion and billing capture and collects consented audio. Phase 2 adds speech models that estimate vocabulary diversity, word combinations and turn-taking latency, giving clinicians a triage report. Phase 3 is a validated FDA pathway.
why_now: Speech models now handle child speech far better than before. Developmental screening is a CMS Child Core Set quality measure (from memory), so Medicaid plans pay for completion. Multimodal models make sample-based scoring feasible.
revenue_model: Per-screen fee or per-provider subscription ($200-500 a month), plus quality-improvement contracts with Medicaid plans, and later a per-report fee.
non_obvious_insight: Parents already record toddlers constantly. The bottleneck is not detection technology but screening completion and triage, so the winning move is to attach to the reimbursed screening code and Medicaid quality measures first and upgrade the signal later.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 independent pediatric practices through a developmental-behavioral pediatrician advisor. Run a 60-day free text-intake screening pilot. Capture consented audio for retrospective validation. Pitch one Medicaid plan's quality team on completion-rate lift.

title: City Micro-Rule API for Group Tour Operators
one_liner: A continuously updated database of group caps, loudspeaker rules, coach drop-off bans, fees and overnight-parking bans across overtouristed places, delivered as an itinerary checker for tour operators and campervan renters.
customer: Small and mid-size group tour operators, DMCs, shore-excursion companies, guide associations and campervan or RV rental firms in Europe.
problem: Cities answer overtourism with many small rules, such as group-size caps and loudspeaker bans in places like Venice and Amsterdam, plus coach access fees and wild-camping bans elsewhere. These live in local-language ordinances, and fines fall on operators and guides. Nobody publishes a single source of truth.
solution: Use multilingual LLM ingestion of municipal ordinances with human legal review for the top 60 cities. The product is an itinerary checker that flags violations and fees, a weekly change digest, an API for booking systems and a WhatsApp bot for guides.
why_now: Municipal crackdowns keep multiplying (Barcelona, Palma, Venice, Amsterdam, the Balearics, Glasgow's levy from Jan 2027). Long-context LLMs make parsing ordinances in many languages cheap only recently.
revenue_model: USD 79-299 per month per operator, enterprise API licences for cruise lines and campervan renters, and paid city packs.
non_obvious_insight: Overtourism policy has fragmented into thousands of tiny local rules. The pain is compliance risk rather than any single rule, and every new rule makes the product more valuable.
first_30_days: Curate rules for 10 cities (for example Venice, Rome, Florence, Amsterdam, Barcelona, Dubrovnik, Lisbon, Athens, Edinburgh and Kyoto) with local guides. Sell 10 operators at USD 99 per month through guide associations, and publish free rules-by-city pages for SEO lead generation.

title: Entry-Integrity Layer for Contests and Festivals
one_liner: Intake screening and a finalist verification desk for photo, film, screenplay and art open calls that fear an AI-winner scandal.
customer: Organizers of photo contests, film festivals, screenwriting and comics competitions, and art open calls, especially those that already collect entry fees through FilmFreeway, Submittable or their own forms.
problem: Generative tools make entries free to produce, so organizers face reviewer overload and reputational risk from an AI-made winner. Platform stigma around AI content has just hardened (TIDAL, Snap, Spotify, YouTube all acted between May and Aug 2026), so a scandal now costs more. Organizers verify nothing beyond a checkbox.
solution: A plugin or service that (1) screens each entry on intake with C2PA and SynthID checks, metadata analysis and a detector ensemble, sorting entries into green, amber and red for screeners, (2) asks finalists for a proof pack (raw files, project files or a behind-the-scenes clip), and (3) runs a 48-hour human-reviewed finalist verification that yields a 'Verified Human-Made Finalist' certificate for the winners' announcement. High-volume calls can add a refundable deposit.
why_now: Provenance signals are now common in cameras and tools, detector prices have fallen, and AI-content policies are stricter across platforms, so organizers finally have something to check against and something to lose.
revenue_model: $0.50-2 per-entry surcharge or $500-5,000 per contest, plus $20-60 per verified finalist, renewing annually.
non_obvious_insight: Organizers already charge entry fees, so a $1 integrity fee is invisible to entrants. Only the top 1-3% of entries need deep verification, and the real buyer motive is insurance against one embarrassing scandal.
first_30_days: List 50 mid-size contests with deadlines in Q4-Q1 from FilmFreeway and photo-contest calendars. Offer free finalist verification to the first five in exchange for a case study, run it as a concierge service with tools behind it, then charge $1,500 flat.

title: Findings Sentinel: A Nurse Tracks Your Scan Follow-Ups
one_liner: What a concierge doctor really sells is closed loops: someone reads every report and owns the follow-up; for $20/mo, a nurse-in-the-loop sentinel makes sure your incidental scan findings do not fall through the cracks.
customer: Adults 50-80 (and their adult children) who had a CT, MRI, ultrasound or pathology in the last three years. Incidentals include lung nodules, thyroid, adrenal and kidney lesions, pancreatic cysts and aneurysms. Secondary buyers are self-insured employers, Medicare Advantage plans and imaging centers that carry follow-up liability.
problem: Studies of incidental findings report follow-up failure rates commonly in the 30-60% range (lung nodules especially). The ordering physician is often not notified beyond the report, the PCP is not copied, and under the Cures Act patients see results in portals before anyone explains them. A concierge doctor reads everything and calls; everyone else gets an unread PDF.
solution: Pull records through patient-directed access (Medicare App Library apps, Apple Health Records, portals) or PDF upload. An LLM extracts each 'recommend follow-up in X months' statement and tracks whether it happened. An RN or NP reviews flagged items and issues a plain-language one-pager with the question to ask and a drafted message or referral request to the PCP. A monthly digest and annual records reconciliation are included. No diagnosis or prescribing, so it is navigation, not telemedicine.
why_now: CMS's Health Tech Ecosystem launched its Medicare App Library in April 2026 with hundreds of organizations pledged to FHIR-based sharing, and TEFCA-style patient access is maturing. LLMs are reliable at extracting follow-up recommendations from radiology text, the same technique hospital nodule programs use. That makes nurse minutes rare and targeted.
revenue_model: $20/mo membership; $99 one-time 'catch-up review' of the last three years; $2-4 per member per month from employers and Medicare Advantage plans; imaging centers pay for closed-loop follow-up as risk reduction. Rough cost basis: extraction costs pennies and, if about 8% of members are flagged yearly at about 25 nurse minutes, clinical labor is only a few dollars per member per year.
non_obvious_insight: The concierge doctor's value is not the 60-minute visit; it is that a competent person reads every report and owns the loop. Loop closure is an insurance-like utilization problem: about 95% of members have nothing to flag most months, so the pooled cost fits $20/mo. Immediate-release results created a new market for 'someone to tell me what this means and what happens next'.
first_30_days: Manually pilot with 30 volunteers recruited from incidentaloma communities and senior centers. Members upload reports, a contract RN reviews them, and you count unclosed loops. Publish the results ('X% had an unclosed loop') for PR, and use them to sign one imaging center or employer pilot before building the app.

title: Two-Way Kasuhara Desk for Tiny Japanese Businesses
one_liner: A QR-and-LINE 'complaint lane' plus staff backup button that gives micro-businesses the customer-harassment policy, consultation channel and evidence log Japan now requires.
customer: Owners of Japanese businesses with 1-100 employees that face customers in person (izakaya, clinics, salons, cram schools, taxi and care operators, retail). They pay ¥2,980-9,800 per site per month. Resale channels are sharoushi (labor and social-insurance consultants) and SME insurance agents.
problem: From 1 Oct 2026 every Japanese employer with at least one employee must publish a policy against customer harassment ('kasuhara'), set up and publicize a consultation channel, and have response procedures. There is no phase-in. Most tiny firms have no HR function, no policy and no channel. Staff also hesitate to report incidents. Customers, for their part, now hesitate to voice legitimate complaints.
solution: (1) A QR code at the counter, on receipts and on LINE opens a structured, polite complaint form (what happened, photo, desired resolution). The owner gets a timestamped record, and abusive or threatening messages are flagged. (2) A 'need backup' button in LINE gives frontline staff an anonymous route to a partner sharoushi or counselor. That route is the required consultation channel. (3) A one-tap incident log that creates a dated evidence pack (notes, optional call-recording notice, response taken). (4) A policy, poster and work-rule addendum generator that meets the MHLW guideline. (5) A monthly 'compliance proof' PDF for the day the labor bureau asks.
why_now: The MHLW guideline was published on 26 Feb 2026 and the duty takes effect 1 Oct 2026, three days from today. Incumbent tooling targets call centers, such as SoftBank's SoftVoice AI voice-softener launched Feb 2026. Nothing is priced or packaged for a 5-person restaurant. The Oct 1 news cycle will also push owners to search for a fix.
revenue_model: ¥2,980/month per site (¥9,800 for 10+ staff), ¥30,000 optional setup for work-rule revision, and a 30% recurring rev-share to sharoushi and insurance agents who resell it. A later upsell is per-incident counselor escalation. Insurers may white-label it into SME liability packages.
non_obvious_insight: The law has a hidden chilling effect on the customer side. In the Channel Corporation survey (497 customer-facing employees plus 514 consumers, June 2026), 52.3% of consumers who hit a store error 'let it pass' for fear of being labelled a harasser, and 65.2% wanted AI-mediated ways to raise issues. A product that gives customers a legitimate complaint lane defuses harassment at the source and doubles as the mandatory paper trail. Enforcement is guidance and then naming rather than fines, so buyers want the cheapest defensible record, not AI detection. Only under 10% of firms use technical measures. Evidence: KiteRa survey of 965 workers on 10-11 Sep 2026 found 61.3% with no policy, 68.3% with no publicized channel, 58.6% of firms with 100 or fewer employees with no channel at all, and 19.8% of workers harassed in the past year, of whom 74.9% hesitated to report (https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000130.000045846.html). Channel Corp found 51.7% with no measures at all (https://ecnomikata.com/ecnews/customerservice/51126/). Legal scope and enforcement: https://www.twobirds.com/en/insights/2026/singapore/customer-harassment-prevention-now-a-statutory-obligation-for-employers-in-japan. Incumbent focus on call centers: https://www.softbank.jp/en/sbnews/entry/20260219_01.
first_30_days: Days 1-3: Ship a free policy-and-poster generator plus a LINE Official Account to catch Oct 1 search traffic, and a landing page in Japanese. Days 4-14: Recruit 5-10 sharoushi (offer 30% recurring share and a white-label report) and 2 local shokokai chambers; sell 'compliance by Friday' to their existing clients. Build the QR complaint form with LINE Messaging API (no app needed) and manually route staff-backup messages to one partner counselor. Days 15-30: Sign 30-50 shops at ¥2,980 and collect 3 named case studies. Ask an SME insurance agency to pilot a bundled offer.

title: The 3 A.M. Pharmacist Desk for Konbini
one_liner: A neutral, multilingual, 24-hour remote pharmacist service that issues the emailed certificate the new law will require before konbini without pharmacists can sell OTC drugs.
customer: Convenience-store owners, first independents and multi-chain franchisees in tourist and nightlife areas of Osaka such as Namba, Dotonbori, Shinsekai and Umeda, then chains. Hotels and hostels are a second channel. Stores pay per certificate, or by sharing the margin on OTC sales.
problem: After 11pm, people keep coming in asking for painkillers, stomach medicine, cold medicine, motion-sickness pills, period-pain relief and allergy tablets. Most Type 2 OTC drugs can only be sold when a registered seller is on the premises, and night staff do not have that license. I turn away a steady stream of tourists and night workers every night. Foreign visitors cannot get counseling in their own language even when a pharmacy is open. That is lost margin and a real public-health gap.
solution: Customers scan a QR code on the shelf, choose products, and join a 60-90 second video or chat consultation in Japanese, English, Chinese, Korean or Vietnamese with a licensed pharmacist. They receive a certificate by email or app, and the clerk verifies it on a phone-based web page before ringing up the sale. The pharmacist network is staffed by night-capable remote pharmacists, such as parents and retirees working from home. The operator holds the pharmacy license and takes on regulatory and liability responsibility. Pre-2027, the same desk runs a limited service on quasi-drugs and pharmacy-hours referral lists so the network and the store workflow are ready when the rule takes effect.
why_now: The amended Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act passed in May 2025. It allows convenience stores without pharmacists or registered sellers to sell OTC drugs after the buyer gets an online pharmacist explanation and an emailed certificate. It takes effect around spring 2027. Lawson has said it plans OTC delivery at stores without pharmacists starting in 2026. Inbound tourism to Osaka remains at record levels. The window for a neutral operator is the next 6-9 months, before chains sign exclusive deals.
revenue_model: ¥300-500 per certificate paid by the store, or 25-30% of the OTC gross margin. Hotels and hostels pay a subscription for guest access. Later revenue comes from manufacturers paying for education and sampling inside consultations, and from chains licensing the network.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for konbini OTC is not shelf space, POS integration or the law. It is a supply of licensed humans awake at 3 a.m., speaking Vietnamese or Chinese, who can explain a drug in 90 seconds. Chains will assume they can build this in-house, but they lack pharmacist labor and multilingual night coverage. A neutral network that any owner can join in an afternoon has the advantage, because independent and multi-chain owners have no other option.
first_30_days: Partner with one licensed Osaka pharmacy, or set up the pharmacy entity, and recruit 10-15 remote pharmacists for night and weekend slots. Build the QR, video, certificate and clerk-verification flow as a web app, tested at my three stores on quasi-drugs and referral flow. Pre-sign letters of intent with 10 owners for spring 2027 pricing. Approach two hotels near Namba for guest access. Meet the health-center pharmacy inspection office to confirm the compliance path before launch.

title: Community Radio as a Paid Knowledge API
angle: AI agents & the agent economy x Emerging markets leapfrogging
one_liner: Turn African community-radio call-in shows into a live, district-level, per-call-priced local-truth feed that farm agents and lenders pay for, with stations keeping most of the revenue.
customer: Agri-input distributors, crop insurers, agri-lenders and farmer-facing AI agents (FarmerChat-style services) in East Africa. Community radio stations in Uganda and Kenya are the supply side and get 70% of revenue.
problem: Western models 'fail spectacularly' on African crops, and satellites cannot see this week's pest outbreak, local planting window or market price. Community radio is where farmers self-report and where trusted extension voices answer, but its ad revenue is collapsing. Bots do not click ads, so stations earn nothing when agents consume their knowledge.
solution: Transcribe and structure weekly call-in shows (Luganda, Swahili, Hausa and others) into dated, sourced, district-level signals such as pest reports, price quotes and planting advice, with provenance and consent. Expose them as an MCP or HTTP endpoint with per-call micropayments via x402 or MPP. Add a paid 'ask the station' tier where an agent's question is read on air and the answer captured. Stations receive rev-share via mobile money.
why_now: Small ASR models (300M-1.7B parameters) now handle local languages, and AethexAI already trains on radio audio. FarmerChat has answered 8M+ questions, which proves demand. Machine-payment protocols make micro-charging per call possible, and Cloudflare's pay-per-crawl is training content owners to charge bots.
revenue_model: Per-call fees for agents ($0.005-0.05), district-level monthly subscriptions ($200-600) for lenders and insurers, and premium on-air Q&A. Platform keeps 30% and stations get 70%.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not a language training set, which is a commodity. It is fresh local ground truth with a trusted human voice behind it, delivered as a live feed rather than an archive. Radio stations are the last network where farmers report in their own words. Content owners who cannot win the ad economy can win the agent-query economy.
first_30_days: Sign 3-5 stations in Uganda and Kenya with a simple rev-share and consent agreement. Record and transcribe two weeks of shows with a fine-tuned open ASR model. Publish a weekly district JSON feed. Sell the first two district subscriptions to an agri-lender or seed distributor at $300-500 a month.

title: Dead Capital: Succession Kits for Diaspora Families
one_liner: A flat-fee, advocate-supervised 'estate file' service that gets a dead parent's or grandfather's land, shares and dormant accounts legally transferred, sold to the adult children who pay from Nairobi, Dallas or Dubai.
customer: Salaried urban and diaspora Kenyans aged 30-55 whose rural parents or grandparents died (or are old) with land still registered in a dead person's name. They pay from abroad or from the city. A secondary B2B payer is any SACCO, coop or bank that needs cleared successions before it releases deposits or lends against land.
problem: Most rural family land is still titled to a dead grandfather or father because nobody completed succession. The process needs a chief's letter, a death certificate, consents from every heir, gazettement, a wait before confirmation of grant, and then transmission at the land registry, which is often 1-3 years and many trips. Until it is done the land cannot be leased, mortgaged, subdivided or cleanly sold, siblings fight, and the deceased's SACCO deposits, coop shares, insurance and pension sit unclaimed. The real blocker is coordinating 8 to 20 relatives to sign, not the court.
solution: Wedge product is a 'Family Estate Map' for roughly KES 15-25k (pricing to be tested). The child sends photos of the title, IDs, death certificate and old share certificates over WhatsApp. An LLM pipeline extracts names and parcel numbers, handles the multiple-name and spelling-variant problem in Kenyan naming, builds the family tree and likely heirs, and lists the consents needed. It runs official land searches and asset-discovery letters to SACCOs, coops, insurers and the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority, then outputs a court-ready bundle of forms and affidavits. A home-county field agent collects the chief's letter and relatives' signatures or thumbprints, with video proof of consent. Partner advocates then file and shepherd the case at their own scale fees. Later upsells are surveyor subdivision and lease or loan readiness.
why_now: The generation that took up land in the 1960s-80s through settlement schemes and land-buying companies is dying now, so the succession backlog is peaking. Diaspora remittances are near record levels (roughly US$5bn a year), and families increasingly ask 'sort out the land' rather than 'build a house'. Digitised land records (Ardhisasa) and court e-filing reduce physical running, though their current coverage needs checking. LLMs can now read messy scanned title and ID documents and draft forms in English while chatting with clients in Swahili. I could not run live searches, so verify current UFAA agent rules, court e-filing scope for successions, and fee schedules before building.
revenue_model: Flat fee per estate file, paid by M-Pesa or card from abroad. Advocate fees are billed by the advocates themselves, so the company sells software and case management and does not split fees with non-lawyers. Asset discovery is a flat add-on fee, not a percentage cut of UFAA payouts, because UFAA discourages middlemen taking a share. B2B revenue is per cleaned member estate from SACCOs and coops. Later there is referral income from surveyors and land-backed lenders once titles are clean.
non_obvious_insight: Rural Kenya's biggest pool of unused collateral is land trapped in the name of the dead. The bottleneck is family coordination and evidence gathering, so the product is a coordination workflow sold to the sibling who has money and guilt, not a land registry or a lawyer marketplace. VCs looking at land-tech miss that the payer is the diaspora child, not the farmer.
first_30_days: Pick one county (for example Murang'a or Kakamega) and recruit two advocates who already do succession work. Build intake on WhatsApp Business, Airtable and an LLM extraction script. Sell 10 files at a pilot discount through your own family network, church and alumni groups, and diaspora WhatsApp and Facebook groups such as Kenyans in Texas or the UK. Publish a free 'Is your family land still in a dead man's name?' checker as lead-gen. Track days from intake to gazettement as the core metric.

title: Reefer Claim Vault for Small Carriers
one_liner: An always-on evidence recorder that captures the proof that decides cargo claims, giving small carriers and their cargo insurers a one-click defense packet.
customer: Small reefer and dry-van carriers (1 to 50 trucks), especially produce and protein lanes, and the cargo-insurance agencies and MGAs that write them. Brokers needing reefer-specific carrier diligence are a secondary buyer.
problem: Small carriers lose or pay $5k to $60k cargo claims not because they were at fault but because they can't prove it. Pre-cool temperature, setpoint, continuous versus cycle-sentry mode, who loaded and counted, and seal integrity all decide a Carmack claim, and the evidence is usually never captured or gets overwritten on the reefer unit. After a claim, the cargo insurer raises rates or cancels. Post-Montgomery, reefer-specific vetting is also becoming a standard-of-care question for brokers.
solution: A driver app with a 90-second guided pickup ritual: photo of the empty trailer floor and reefer display, pre-cool temp, setpoint and mode, seal photo before the forklift touches it, an OCR check of the BOL that flags a missing 'SL&C' (shipper load and count) notation, seal number or temp instructions, and a Bluetooth probe reading of product temperature at load. It pulls continuous temperature records from reefer telematics (Thermo King, Carrier) or a $30 BLE data logger and hash-timestamps everything. When a claim lands, it generates a Carmack-structured defense packet in one click. Insurers get aggregate loss-prevention scoring by carrier.
why_now: The 2026 Montgomery ruling has brokers and insurers paying attention to reefer diligence. Cargo losses and theft are up sharply (Verisk CargoNet Q2 2026 losses of $304.6M). Vision AI makes BOL and photo checking cheap, and reefer telematics APIs and cheap Bluetooth loggers have matured.
revenue_model: $25 to $40 per truck per month for carriers. MGAs and agencies pay $10 per truck per month or fund the subscription in exchange for loss-ratio improvement and premium credits. A $150 flat fee per claim-defense packet for non-subscribers as a low-friction entry.
non_obvious_insight: Claims are decided by paper nobody produced in the sixty seconds when it mattered. Every veteran knows the ritual: write SL&C on the BOL, photograph the seal before anyone touches the door, snap the pre-cool, and download the reefer unit before it rolls over. Nobody does it consistently because nobody reminds them at the dock. Insurers see the losses but not the cause, so they will pay to change driver behavior at the moment of pickup.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 small cargo-insurance agencies that specialize in trucking. Recruit 20 reefer carriers hauling produce (Fresno to Nogales, Yakima, Salinas). Give them a free 30-day pilot plus the BLE logger at cost. Build a PWA using photo capture and Claude vision for BOL checks. Track claim outcomes on pilot trucks versus a control group to build the insurer's business case.

title: Fire-Loss Data Co-op and Parametric MRF Cover
one_liner: Pool waste-facility fire data to price the unpriced battery-fire risk, then offer verified premium credits and fast-paying parametric cover.
customer: MRFs, transfer stations, scrap yards and e-scrap recyclers (pay verification and premium), with specialty brokers, MGAs and reinsurers buying the data.
problem: August 2026 saw 49 facility fires (tied for the 10-year August high), 293 year to date, and 74 catastrophic (over $400K) versus 71 in all of 2024. Public counts cover only two-alarm-plus events, and actual totals may be about 6x higher. Severe incidents average about $1.5M and no one has decided who pays.
solution: Step 1 is a fire-risk score and controls-verification certificate (thermal cameras, suppression, inbound inspection, tip-floor separation). Step 2 is an anonymized incident and thermal-alert data co-op. Step 3 is an MGA arrangement with a fronting carrier offering premium credits for verified controls and a parametric top-up that pays a fixed amount when a verified thermal event crosses a threshold, for fast cleanup and business-interruption cash.
why_now: Losses are concentrating and rising, states are still arguing about liability, and BRACE Act storage-permit debates put battery handling in the spotlight. The expected next step is insurers repricing, adding exclusions or demanding sensors, so verified data becomes the currency.
revenue_model: $2-5K per site per year for verification, a 10-15% MGA commission on placed premium, and data licensing to insurers and reinsurers.
non_obvious_insight: The unpriced risk here is data, not fire physics. The industry's own public numbers understate reality by roughly 6x, so the first party with a real loss dataset sets the price.
first_30_days: Compile a scrubbed fire dataset from trackers, news, fire-department reports and OSHA logs and derive loss-cost bands. Interview 5 specialty brokers. Recruit 5 facilities for a pilot with an off-the-shelf thermal camera package. Open talks with a fronting carrier.

title: DIC Finder for Veteran Families at Funerals
one_liner: A tool that reads a veteran's death certificate, hospice diagnosis and DD-214 to spot survivor benefits the widow does not know exist, sold to funeral homes and hospices rather than to families.
customer: Funeral homes (roughly 18,000 to 19,000 in the U.S.) that want a differentiated service for veteran families, and hospices with veteran programs. State veteran departments and accredited service officers are downstream partners.
problem: The Vietnam-era generation is now in the last phase of life and forms a large share of veteran deaths. The PACT Act (2022) expanded presumptive conditions for Agent Orange, burn pit and other exposures, so many widows may qualify for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC, on the order of $1,700 a month, check the current rate). Others may qualify for the Aid and Attendance survivor pension, or accrued benefits. Most never file. The death certificate says 'cardiac arrest' or 'respiratory failure' rather than the underlying service-connected condition. The funeral director's VA paperwork is only for the flag, headstone and burial allowance, and nobody reads the chart for exposure history. The hospice chaplain hears the veteran's service story at the bedside and the widow's money worries at the kitchen table, but has no tool to connect them.
solution: A web and mobile intake tool run at the arrangement conference or at the hospice bereavement visit. It photographs the DD-214, asks a 5-minute exposure and service history (deployment dates and locations, unit, conditions), and matches them against presumptive-condition and location lists. It flags likely DIC, survivor pension and accrued-benefit eligibility, and pre-fills VA Form 21P-534EZ. It then hands the case, with a warm introduction, to an accredited VSO representative or an accredited claims agent. The tool also stores the veteran's story fields so a funeral home can honor the person accurately.
why_now: The PACT Act has created a large wave of newly presumptive conditions, and claim volumes at the VA are at record levels. Vietnam-era veterans are aging into their peak mortality years. As I understand VA rules, accredited representatives can only charge fees after an initial decision, and legislation to tighten fees on predatory claim sharks has been moving. That pushes the sustainable model toward a B2B payer, not families. AI document extraction now makes DD-214 and death-certificate parsing cheap and reliable. Confirm current DIC rates and fee rules before launch.
revenue_model: SaaS for funeral homes at $149 to $299 a month per location, with a per-case add-on for premium processing. Hospices and state veteran departments pay a per-completed-referral fee or a flat annual license. The VSO or accredited-agent partner pays for qualified leads only where the rules allow it, so this must be reviewed by counsel. Families pay nothing.
non_obvious_insight: The money is unclaimed not because widows are lazy but because the trigger event is the funeral, and the only professional in the room (the funeral director) has no financial incentive or training to read a service history. Funeral homes will pay to look like heroes to veteran families, since it feeds pre-need referrals for the next generation, which is where their margin lives.
first_30_days: Partner with one accredited county veteran service officer and two independent funeral homes near a large veteran population. Build the intake as a form plus a manual review by the VSO in week one, before any automation. Run 15 real cases at no charge and record dollars unlocked per family. Use those numbers to close five paying funeral homes at $149 a month. Have a veterans-law attorney review the fee and referral structure before charging anyone.

title: Phage Red-Teaming and Immunity Stacks for Fermenters
one_liner: Penetration-test production strains with adversarially evolved phages, then harden them with stacked, AI-selected anti-phage defenses.
customer: Industrial fermentation operators and CDMOs running E. coli, Bacillus, Corynebacterium or Streptomyces hosts for recombinant proteins, enzymes, amino acids and precision-fermentation ingredients.
problem: Phage contamination can cause widespread fermentation failure and lingering facility contamination, and outages are usually hidden. Dairy lactic-acid strains have phage-resistance programs, but most other production hosts do not. Academic work shows phage-resistant E. coli is feasible (Nature Communications 2022; CRISPR-immunity work in 2025), yet nobody sells it as a service.
solution: (1) Surveillance: metagenomic sequencing of broth and environmental swabs for phage signatures. (2) Red team: isolate and evolve escape phages against the customer's strain in a BSL-1/2 lab, extending the search with AI-designed phage genomes. (3) Hardening: stack defense modules (restriction-modification, CRISPR, abortive infection), test them, and deliver a strain with unchanged titer.
why_now: Arc Institute and Stanford used Evo genome language models to write phage genomes: 16 viable phages from about 300 designs, and a cocktail that cleared E. coli resistant to the natural template. DNA synthesis costs have collapsed, so testing dozens of defense combinations is cheap. Precision fermentation and biologic capacity is scaling.
revenue_model: $2-6k/month per site for surveillance, $25-60k per red-team audit, and $150-400k per hardened strain as a license fee without royalties.
non_obvious_insight: Phage risk is treated as bad luck. Treating it like cybersecurity, with continuous monitoring plus adversarial testing, creates a budget line. Operators hide outages, so the first buyers are CDMO QA leads and insurers who need proof of resilience.
first_30_days: Offer a free phage-susceptibility screen of environmental swabs to 5 precision-fermentation startups. Build a library of 30 defense modules for E. coli and Bacillus. Sign 2 paid audits ($15-25k). Complete a biosafety review of the adversarial-phage protocol.

title: AV-TEST for Deepfake and Liveness Detectors
one_liner: A buyer-funded independent lab that red-teams deepfake and liveness detectors every month against fresh in-the-wild fakes and publishes procurement-grade scorecards.
customer: Bank and insurer model-risk and fraud-procurement teams, enterprise CISOs buying detection, media organizations, and expert witnesses. All buy annual subscriptions.
problem: Enterprise detection and IDV are the most crowded categories in the brief, and every vendor claims 95-99% accuracy on its own test set. Buyers cannot compare products. Accuracy decays with each new generator, and injection attacks bypass isolated liveness checks. Model-risk officers must validate vendor models but have no independent evidence.
solution: Maintain a continuously refreshed attack corpus: newly released generators, voice clones degraded through phone codecs, virtual-camera and emulator injection, and re-compressed video. Test vendors black-box via API and publish false-accept rates at fixed false-reject rates, cross-generator drift, and time-to-fail after each new model release. Add model-risk documentation packs and court-ready error-rate statements. Vendors may pay only for private testing, never for ranking.
why_now: Detection vendors multiplied in 2025-26 and funding is still flowing (Modulate raised $25M). The injection-attack standard CEN/TS 18099 exists but has almost no commercial third-party lab. The EU AI Act transparency deadline on 2 Dec 2026 and rising fraud losses push buyers to demand proof.
revenue_model: $15-60K per year for full scorecards and monthly refreshes. Custom bake-offs for $25-100K. Expert-witness and litigation support as an upsell.
non_obvious_insight: In the 1990s, antivirus claims were unverifiable until independent labs became the arbiter. Deepfake detection is worse because accuracy decays with every new generator, so buyers need continuous evidence, which is a recurring-revenue product. The real asset is the fresh, hard-to-game attack corpus, and no vendor can build it credibly for itself.
first_30_days: Publish a free baseline report on 10 public detectors using about 300 fresh fakes from the newest open and commercial generators. Send it to 30 bank model-risk leads. Sign 3-5 design-partner subscriptions at about $10K each.
